items.example: She's not really a friend, more of a frenemy.
items.exampleTr: O aslında arkadaş değil, daha çok dost kılığında düşman.
items.simple: Someone who acts like your friend but secretly wants you to lose.
dialogue: A: Are you inviting Chloe?
B: I have to. She's my office frenemy.
items.note: friend + enemy; gayriresmî, esprili.

items.tr: (birini) aniden yok saymak, mesajlara cevap vermeyip ortadan kaybolmak
items.example: We went on three dates and then he ghosted me.
items.exampleTr: Üç kez buluştuk, sonra bir anda ortadan kayboldu.
items.simple: Stop answering someone's messages and just vanish, with no goodbye.
dialogue: A: Did that guy ever text you back?
B: Nope. Why do people ghost instead of just saying no?
items.note: Flört ve arkadaşlıkta; iş başvurularında da kullanılır.

items.example: He's lovely, but a bit needy, he texts me every hour.
items.exampleTr: Çok tatlı ama biraz ilgi delisi, her saat mesaj atıyor.
items.simple: Someone who always wants your time and attention.
dialogue: A: Is your new cat friendly?
B: Too friendly. She's so needy.
items.note: İlişki ve arkadaşlıkta olumsuz; 'clingy' ile yakın.

items.example: Her 'per my last email' was very passive-aggressive.
items.exampleTr: 'Son e-postamda belirttiğim üzere' demesi çok pasif-agresifti.
items.simple: Being angry in a quiet, sneaky way instead of saying it.
dialogue: A: My flatmate left a note: 'Hope you enjoyed MY milk.'
B: Wow, that's so passive-aggressive.
items.note: Ofis yazışmalarında ve ev arkadaşı notlarında çok kullanılır.

items.example: We're a tight-knit family, we talk every day.
items.exampleTr: Birbirimize çok bağlı bir aileyiz, her gün konuşuruz.
items.simple: A small group of people who are very close and help each other.
dialogue: A: Is it hard being new in the village?
B: A bit. It's a tight-knit community.
items.note: Aile, ekip, mahalle için.

items.example: She seemed standoffish at first, but she's just shy.
items.exampleTr: İlk başta mesafeli görünüyordu ama sadece utangaç.
items.simple: Not friendly, keeps away from people and doesn't chat.
dialogue: A: What do you think of the new neighbour?
B: Bit standoffish, to be honest.
items.note: Genelde ilk izlenim için; 'aloof'tan daha gündelik.

items.example: They had a falling-out over money and haven't spoken since.
items.exampleTr: Para yüzünden araları bozuldu ve o günden beri konuşmuyorlar.
items.simple: A fight that makes two friends stop being friends for a while.
dialogue: A: Aren't you and Kate friends anymore?
B: We had a bit of a falling-out last year.
items.note: 'have a falling-out with someone' kalıbı; fiili 'fall out'.

items.example: My ex was really high-maintenance.
items.exampleTr: Eski sevgilim gerçekten çok nazlıydı.
items.simple: Someone who needs lots of time, care and attention all the time.
dialogue: A: Your new puppy is adorable.
B: Adorable, but very high-maintenance.
items.note: Kişi, evcil hayvan, bitki için; tersi 'low-maintenance'.

items.example: When I lost my job, I found out who the fair-weather friends were.
items.exampleTr: İşimi kaybedince kimlerin iyi gün dostu olduğunu anladım.
items.simple: A friend who stays only when things are good, and leaves when things go bad.
dialogue: A: Has Lee called since you got ill?
B: No. Turns out he's a fair-weather friend.
items.note: 'fair-weather fan' = sadece kazanınca destekleyen taraftar.

items.example: There was an awkward silence after he mentioned his ex.
items.exampleTr: Eski sevgilisinden bahsedince garip bir sessizlik oldu.
items.simple: When nobody talks and everyone feels a bit uncomfortable.
dialogue: A: How did the dinner with your in-laws go?
B: Let's just say there was an awkward silence or two.
items.note: Çok yaygın; 'cue awkward silence' esprili kullanım.

items.example: I decided to offer an olive branch and invite her for coffee.
items.exampleTr: Barış eli uzatıp onu kahveye davet etmeye karar verdim.
items.simple: Do something kind to show you want to stop fighting.
dialogue: A: You're still not talking to your brother?
B: I think it's time to offer an olive branch.
items.note: 'extend an olive branch' de denir.

items.example: There's been bad blood between the two families for years.
items.exampleTr: İki aile arasında yıllardır husumet var.
items.simple: Old anger between people that hasn't gone away.
dialogue: A: Why won't they sit at the same table?
B: There's a lot of bad blood there.
items.note: 'There's bad blood between them' kalıbı.

items.en: the black sheep of the family
items.example: My uncle is the black sheep of the family.
items.exampleTr: Amcam ailenin yüz karası sayılır.
items.simple: The one person in a family who is very different, often in a bad way.
dialogue: A: Why does nobody talk about your cousin?
B: He's the black sheep of the family.
items.note: Bazen gururla: 'I'm the black sheep, I became an artist.'

items.example: Can I bring a plus-one to the wedding?
items.exampleTr: Düğüne yanımda birini getirebilir miyim?
items.simple: The extra person you can bring with you to a party or wedding.
dialogue: A: Are you bringing anyone to the party?
B: Yeah, my sister's my plus-one.
items.note: Davetiyede 'John + 1' gibi yazılır; 'my plus-one' = eşlikçim.

items.example: She didn't reply with a kiss, but don't read too much into it.
items.exampleTr: Mesajını öpücüksüz göndermiş ama fazla anlam yükleme.
items.simple: Think something means more than it really does.
dialogue: A: He said 'ok.' with a full stop. Is he angry?
B: I wouldn't read too much into it.
items.note: Mesaj, bakış, söz yorumlarken çok kullanılır.

items.example: I've always had a soft spot for my little cousin.
items.exampleTr: Küçük kuzenime hep ayrı bir zaafım olmuştur.
items.simple: Like someone or something a lot, even if you don't know why.
dialogue: A: Why do you let him get away with everything?
B: I just have a soft spot for him.
items.note: Kişi, yemek, eski şarkı için.

items.example: Those two are joined at the hip, you never see one without the other.
items.exampleTr: O ikisi yapışık gibi, birini diğeri olmadan göremezsin.
items.simple: Two people who are always together.
dialogue: A: Is Amy coming?
B: If Ben's coming, yes. They're joined at the hip.
items.note: Hafif esprili; bazen 'biraz fazla' anlamında.

items.example: My sister and I are not on speaking terms right now.
items.exampleTr: Kız kardeşimle şu an küsüz.
items.simple: Two people are so angry that they don't talk to each other.
dialogue: A: Is your dad coming to the wedding?
B: Not sure. He and my mum are not on speaking terms.
items.note: 'back on speaking terms' = barıştılar.

items.en: put a brave face on it
items.example: She's heartbroken, but she's putting a brave face on it.
items.exampleTr: Kalbi kırık ama belli etmiyor.
items.simple: Look happy and strong even when you feel sad inside.
dialogue: A: How's Tom coping after the break-up?
B: He's trying to put a brave face on it.
items.note: 'put on a brave face' de denir.

items.example: Neither of them wants to make the first move.
items.exampleTr: İkisi de ilk adımı atmak istemiyor.
items.simple: Be the one who starts, like texting first or saying sorry first.
dialogue: A: Just text him!
B: No way, I'm not going to make the first move.
items.note: Flörtte ve barışmada; 'Who made the first move?'

items.tr: bana kin tutmak, (bunu) bana karşı kullanmak
items.example: I forgot your birthday, please don't hold it against me.
items.exampleTr: Doğum gününü unuttum, lütfen bana kırılma.
items.simple: Stay angry at someone for a long time because of one thing.
dialogue: A: Sorry I missed your party. Please don't hold it against me.
B: Don't be silly, it's fine.
items.note: 'me' kişiye göre değişir: 'I won't hold it against you.'

items.example: We just clicked, we're totally on the same wavelength.
items.exampleTr: Hemen anlaştık, tamamen aynı frekanstayız.
items.simple: Two people who think and feel the same way, so they understand each other.
dialogue: A: How's the new flatmate?
B: Great. We're on the same wavelength about everything.
items.note: Arkadaşlık ve iş ortaklığında.

items.tr: seni ezip geçmek, sana istediğini yaptırmak
items.example: If you always say yes, people will walk all over you.
items.exampleTr: Hep evet dersen insanlar seni ezer geçer.
items.simple: Treat you badly because they know you won't say no.
dialogue: A: My boss gave me another weekend shift.
B: You can't let him walk all over you.
items.note: 'Don't let them walk all over you' kalıbı çok yaygın.

items.example: You can't just leave me hanging like that, what happened next?
items.exampleTr: Beni öyle merakta bırakamazsın, sonra ne oldu?
items.simple: Not answer or not finish something, so someone is left waiting.
dialogue: A: I'll tell you the rest tomorrow.
B: Don't leave me hanging!
items.note: Çak/high five'a karşılık vermeyince de: 'Don't leave me hanging!'

items.tr: bir sıcak bir soğuk davranmak, kararsız olmak
items.example: He keeps blowing hot and cold about moving in together.
items.exampleTr: Birlikte taşınma konusunda bir sıcak bir soğuk davranıyor.
items.simple: Be keen one day and not interested the next day.
dialogue: A: Is she interested in the job or not?
B: She seems to blow hot and cold.
items.note: İlişki veya karar konusunda kararsızlık.

items.example: It's time you mended fences with your dad.
items.exampleTr: Babanla aranı düzeltmenin zamanı geldi.
items.simple: Fix a friendship after a fight.
dialogue: A: You're having lunch with Sarah? I thought you'd fallen out.
B: We're trying to mend fences.
items.note: 'mend fences with someone' kalıbı.
